text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Government lifts ban on ADC airline, whose Boeing 727 aircraft crashed on November 7 killing all 142 people on board.
- Police arrest senior airport security official one day after linking the opposition to car bomb explosion two weeks ago near Lagos airport in which three people were killed.
- Nigeria and Russia to sign accord on combating drug trafficking, says chief anti-narcotics officer Major-General Musa Bamaiyi.
- Political parties begin mobilising for local council poll despite fears the election may not take place in December as originally scheduled.
- Failed Banks tribunal acquits two six people charged with stealing 34.8 million naira from the African Continental Bank.
- Korean jeep Musso, made by Ssang Yong Motor Company of South Korea launched in Nigerian market amidst fanfare.

- Nigeria's Shooting Stars football club vow to avenge 1984 defeat by Egypt's Zamalek when they meet again on Saturday in the first-leg final of the African champions cup competition in Ibadan, southwestern Nigeria.
